items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: You had you know Art Blakey and of course Thelonious Monk, Max Roach, you had these great musicians that were still here

ctx.x: This is a sort of a tough question but you’ve been involved in jazz for a long time. We spoke about your time with Charles Mingus and having your own bands all these years. And then you just spoke about playing a jazz festival like three weeks ago in Upstate New York. Can you think about the biggest changes you’ve noticed in jazz and the business of jazz between that time back in the sixties and now?

Well yeah, that’s — I think there — you know I think there might be more genres of jazz maybe now than before. In the sixties you had the influence of Charlie Mingus, people like John Coltrane, the avante garde was happening you know, Ornette was there. You had you know Art Blakey and of course Thelonious Monk, Max Roach, you had these great musicians that were still here and everybody had their own style but I think now the difference is there just might be more different offshoots of jazz. Or people that play…

I mean the actual quality and level of musicianship and artistry, you know the sixties and even before that had very high levels of musicianship and artistry you know. That didn’t start with the sixties, that’s always been around. And now you — I’ll tell you what is different, academia is different. There are more schools — high schools, colleges — that have jazz programs. That wasn’t quite like that in the sixties and of course earlier. So that’s different, so therefore it’s producing younger players, you know…
